alignments.note: Waw of the casuistic protasis takes the ASV's And (rule 14).
נֶפֶשׁ rendered by the indefinite 'any one'; the supplied determiner 'any' joins the nominal under rule 15 and the head stays on the word carrying the lexeme.
כִּי takes the ASV's temporal subordinator 'when' (rules 14, 55).
Finite verb with its own English verb.
Indefinite article belongs to the noun it determines (rule 15).

Nomen rectum of the construct chain takes the relational 'of' (rule 19); 'a' joins the nominal by rule 15. Head on 'offering'; 'meal offering' is the ASV's fixed two-word rendering of מִנְחָה and 'meal' alone is never written for it, so the alternative head on 'meal' was rejected.
Preposition לְ rendered 'unto'.
Divine name.

Predicate nominal with a supplied 'of' licensed by the noun's own predicative function (rule 33). Head on 'fine' by rule 31's tie-break: the ASV never writes bare 'flour' for a Hebrew word of this class (it writes 'meal' for קֶמַח), so 'flour' is the supplied generic. The competing reading heads on 'flour'.
הָיָה with its auxiliary; head on the copular verb.
Construct noun keeps only its own word.
Suffix takes the possessive pronoun (rule 18).
Waw of the consecutive form takes 'and' (rule 14).
Subject pronoun and auxiliary join the verb (rule 17); head on the lexical verb.
עַל rendered 'upon'.
Suffix takes the object pronoun.
Object noun.
Waw takes 'and'.
Verb; the ASV gaps the subject and auxiliary here.
Preposition plus its own suffix fused in the single word 'thereon' (rule 30, as rule 22 reads בָּהּ → therein); headed on the preposition.
Object noun.

review_notes: Parallel clauses: the first עָלֶיהָ is rendered analytically 'upon it' and the second synthetically 'thereon'; each is aligned as written rather than harmonized.
סֹלֶת headed on 'fine' throughout the chapter; the competing head on 'flour' is named in the unit note.
